name: dsh-vscode
description: Runs the DeepSeek Harness web surface inside VS Code. All host dependencies are bundled into the extension — users need no Node.js, npm, pnpm, or Python.

dsh.openOnStartup.description: Open the Harness panel automatically when a trusted workspace window starts.

dsh.cwd.description: Working directory for the DSH host (the agent's cwd). Empty = the first workspace folder.

dsh.dshHome.description: Override DSH_HOME (profiles, settings, sessions). Empty = the DSH default.

dsh.enableBakedPlugins.description: Mount the ecosystem plugins baked into this extension into the web profile.

dsh.modlensFamilies.markdownDescription:
**Extra** model-id prefixes that `@liustack/modlens` should trust as text-only and bridge with a `(modlens vision)` entry, so a text-only model gets sight.

modlens matches a family as a case-insensitive **prefix** of the model id (after stripping a leading `~` and any `vendor/` namespace), and its own default is `deepseek`, `glm`, `mimo`. Add prefixes here when your provider routes use opaque aliases — for example `code_instuct`, `code_think` on a gateway that hides DeepSeek/GLM behind them.

Your entries are **added to** `deepseek`, `glm`, `mimo`; the built-in three are never dropped. (modlens resolves `config.families || [defaults]`, so a list sent without them would replace them.)

Leave empty to pass no override at all. Prefer naming families explicitly over `*`: a bare `*` additionally requires the model catalog to declare `text` input, which third-party catalogs usually do not.

Changing this value restarts the DSH host.
